image_description: A close-up, slightly low-angle shot of a vintage handheld computer (PDA), likely a Palm Pilot or similar device from the late 90s/early 2000s. The device has a dark grey plastic casing with rounded corners. The screen is covered by a protective layer featuring hand-drawn sketches of landmarks (Eiffel Tower, etc.) and text. Below the screen are four physical circular buttons and a central navigation pad. The background is a blurry, bright lime-green surface.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The handwritten text on the screen protector ('Paris', 'London') is legible but stylistically inconsistent and slightly warped, typical of AI struggling with specific handwriting styles on curved surfaces. The printed text at the bottom of the screen area is also slightly indistinct.
The four circular buttons below the screen lack clear mechanical definition (gaps/seams) and appear slightly fused with the surrounding casing. The specular highlights on them are soft and undefined.

The central oval navigation button has an ambiguous structure. It lacks a clear bezel or separation from the casing, appearing as a painted-on shape rather than a physical, pressable component. The inner details are muddy.
